newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in lacklustre trade, dealers said on Tuesday.
They said news that the United States had launched a missile attack on Iraq had little impact on the market.
Most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. July leading indicators and August National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) index data.

Leading indicators figures for July is forecast to show an increase of 0.2 percent compared with a 0.5 percent gain reported in June. The August NAPM index is expected to rise to 52.9 percent against July's 50.2 percent.

"Rates were mixed in the morning on some position adjustments. Some people are waiting for more clues to market direction from tonight's leading indicators and NAPM index figures," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact here, unless the figures are way off market expectations. Some people are also waiting for this Friday's employment report," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday, Wednesday/Thursday and week-fixed rose 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged from Monday's 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, four-months eased 1/16 point to 5-9/16 5-7/16, six-months was unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/8 6 percent.
